Thinking about this, there's plenty of CPU power out there to make it happen, but the main obstacles would be verification and latency. The work it takes to verify that someone's machine isn't popping back malicious results is comparable to the work in the first place. And when you farm this out to other machines, who's to say that the workers will respond in a reasonable time... or at all? How long do you give the workers to respond before resubmitting that work item?

How do you prevent DDOS by someone connecting several workers and doing nothing with them?

There are all kinds of issues. The thought comes from the right place, but I don't see it happening for these reasons and probably much much more.

This just isn't feasable. Every aspect of this, as a project would be astranomical. The idea is sound, sure, but seti wasn't designed to run a webserver, latency wasn't their prime concern, just getting the job done "as fast as possible." there was no minimum. I often consider, or try to consider, what I think the person knows on the topic. As it were, it's hard to estimate exactly how much a person knows about a given thing, given humans have thus far not evolved telepathy. With that said, it's often possible, given enough time, to assertain the extent to which a person has knowledge on a topic based on your previous experience with them.

For example, when a friend asks "what do you mean, nothing actually touches?" First, I have to go into the linguistic construct and definition for touch. It's often sufficient to explain that many things are defined linguistically that don't necessarily accurately describe what happens in the objective physical world. This is often enough to cause them to stare blankly at me, likely daydreaming about pie, or some such thing.

In the end, it's usually better to...well shit.

But this is not the norm, under normal circumstances I will answer with a simple "yes" or "no". Meaning that under normal circumstances the answer to this question would be "no", even though that is not true.
